about.title: Gonzales Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Gonzales is a small city, but its traffic doesn't stay quiet everywhere. Public crash records show 8 injury collisions and 8 people hurt in the most recent final reporting year, with Fridays between 6 and 8 p.m. showing up most often. Alta Street, 5th Street, US-101, and Fanoe Road carry much of the local flow, and that's where a lot of these collisions happen. If you were injured on one of these roads, the period right after matters: photos fade, skid marks get repaved, and witnesses move on. We handle car accident claims in the Gonzales and Monterey County area and can review what happened and explain your options. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government entity or road condition was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. We can help you figure out which deadline actually applies to your Gonzales crash.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You Fast
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but the insurer will look for any reason to shift blame onto you and lower what they owe. Giving a recorded statement early, before you understand the coverage or fault issues, can hurt you later.

items.title: No Cap on What Pain and Suffering Is Worth
items.desc: California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain, disruption, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. Our team works on contingency and has no incentive to undervalue that side of your claim, since we're only paid if you recover.

items.question: Do I need to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: No, and it's usually better not to until you've spoken with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to reduce or deny your claim. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on US-101 near Gonzales instead of a city street?
items.answer: Highway crashes can involve different insurance layers, higher speeds, and sometimes multiple vehicles, which can complicate fault. We can review the specific location and circumstances, whether it was US-101, Fanoe Road, or a city street like Alta or 5th, and explain how that affects your claim.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost and no obligation to move forward after you speak with us.
